chapter: Savoy days, the Concord and business
title: Small group and the Concord Hotel since 1967
summary: He recounts his first small group and the personnel changes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You had mentioned earlier that in the latter 50's, you began to break your big band down. You went first to smaller versions of the big band, and then eventually to sort of concentrate on smaller groups. And, I notice you've been here at the Concorde Hotel now for how long?

Well, I was trying to recall the first year. The big band, I think it was as I said in the '50's when the small group, I had—I was down to Bobby Smith and Julian Dash on sax, Ace Harris at piano, Sonny Payne was on drums, Lee Stanfield was on bass, and for awhile, Sammy Lowe was with me. You know, he was playing trumpet too, and myself. I think that was the, that was around, that was the first group.
And then, I made it, I had a couple of changes. Let me see. Norris Turney. I Mercer Ellington now, think he's playing with (unintelligible) first alto.

He took Bobby Smith's place. There were a couple of bass players. I can't recall their name cause Stanfield passed soon. Oh, Kelly Martin. You know, Kelly Martin was with me also with the big band, too, for awhile also before he went with the "Misty" man.
Right. Right. He was with me. I got him out of Detroit. He was with me for quite a while.
